LESSON: MINING

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: GEOGRAPHY
Strand: Human and Economic Activities
Topic 3.2: Mining
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 20

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Mining, part of Human and Economic Activities in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 GEOGRAPHY.

Key inquiry question: When writing, they could 1. How can we exploit minerals sustainably? 2. Why should we rehabilitate mining sites?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Brainstorm on the meaning of minerals and mining and share in class, Learners with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication-AAC or be allowed extra time to express their views. Positioning,

2. Carry out a library research to establish occurrence of minerals and make notes.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Brainstorm on the meaning of minerals and mining and share in class, Learners with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication-AAC or be allowed extra time to express their views. Positioning,
2. Carry out a library research to establish occurrence of minerals and make notes.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Mining together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Citizenship: The skill of global awareness as the learner watches documentaries on mining of limestone in

Kenya, diamond in Botswana and iron ore in Australia

● Digital Literacy: The skill of interacting with technology as the learner uses digital resources to research on

methods used in extraction of minerals

● Communication and Collaboration: The skill of writing as the learner writes an article on the effects of mining

on environment and possible solutions and publishes

● Learning to Learn: The skill of sharing is enhanced as learners brainstorm, in pairs, on the meaning of minerals

and mining and share in class.

53

Values:
● Unity: Learner works together to create communication messages on the importance of rehabilitating mining

sites

● Respect: Learner respects opinions of others as they discuss factors influencing occurrence and exploitation of

minerals and presents in class

● Responsibility: Learners use digital resources to research on methods used in extraction of minerals and take

notes.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Self-Awareness: Learner confidently creates communication messages on the importance of rehabilitating

mining sites and displays in the school notice boards

● Environmental Education: Learner participates in writing an article on the effects of mining on environment

and possible solutions and publishes

● Safety and Security: Learners write articles on the effects of mining on the environment.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Photographs, pictures, local and extended environment, maps, manilla papers, digital resources, charts, marker pens,

approved textbooks and other printed resources, library resources, whiteboards, marker pens
